title: Recording with Duke Ellington
summary: He made a date in Philadelphia and a New York all-star recording with Ellington, Sy Oliver and Bill Harris.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you ever work with Duke Ellington at any time?
Yeah, I made a recording. I made a date with him in Philadelphia, spent a weekend there working. Then I made a recording with him in New York.

Had to be in the 30's because we were in the studio and that's when they were having these all-star records. Bill Harris was on one side and I was on the other side. Sy Oliver made an arrangement and Duke made one side. Sy wouldn't give him no solo. Duke said, 'Uh-huh...' That's when we made the first side.
What was the name of it?
He was sitting at the piano and he did like this. I said, 'What is that for?' He said, 'You just play anything you want as long as you get ready. This is your introduction.' And that's what I did.
What was the name of the song?
